articles.title: Foundry Row Gets $7,500 for Community Oven
articles.deck: Residents of Foundry Row filled the hall on Saturday to ask questions about the plan.
body: The group has raised $7,500 so far and is asking for help with supplies and food. Angela Zielinski, who has lived in Foundry Row for 40 years, said the response has been better than anyone expected.
The plan calls for community oven along Laurel Drive, with work expected to start in October.

articles.title: Eastgate Gets $12,000 for Stormwater Drain Repair
articles.deck: The money will be spent over the next year, with the first work starting in February.
body: The group has raised $12,000 so far and is asking for help with supplies and food. The plan calls for stormwater drain repair along Dover Lane, with work expected to start in February.

Kiera Abernathy, who has lived in Eastgate for 40 years, said the response has been better than anyone expected. The Eastgate Improvement Group will post updates on its bulletin board outside the library.
Organizers say the project is on schedule and that volunteers are still needed on Thursday mornings. Public works estimates the work will take about 40 weeks once it begins.

articles.title: Foundry Row Asks Council for Speed Limit Change
articles.deck: Supporters and opponents on Foundry Street disagreed about cost and timing.
body: Public works estimates the work will take about 40 weeks once it starts in July. The ordinance will return to the agenda at the next regular session, unless the chair calls a special meeting first.
Councilmember Wanda Quinlan asked for more time to review the proposal, which would cost about $25,000.

Staff recommended approval with two conditions: a traffic study and a public notice period of 30 days. Residents of Foundry Row said they had been asking for action for years, and several brought photographs of the street.

articles.title: Gordon Lindqvist, 67, Longtime Volunteer
articles.deck: Friends remember Gordon Lindqvist for the many years of service to Hickory Ridge.
body: Born in Hickory Ridge in the years after the war, Gordon Lindqvist spent most of a working life in the trades and most of a retirement in the neighborhood.
Survivors include a daughter, two grandchildren and many friends from Hickory Ridge.

Gordon Lindqvist died in October at home on Carver Drive, at the age of 67. Services will be held at the parish hall, and donations may be made to the Upper Commons Historical Society in his or her name.

articles.title: Sycamore Avenue Repaving Set to Begin in January
articles.deck: The work is expected to take 37 weeks and will be paid for with $1,200 raised locally.
body: The effort began in January when a handful of neighbors met at the Eastgate community hall to talk about streetlight upgrade. The Canal Park Improvement Group will post updates on its bulletin board outside the library.
The group has raised $1,200 so far and is asking for help with supplies and food. Anyone interested can attend the next planning meeting at the Eastgate community hall on Sunday at 7 p.m.

Lorraine Whitcomb, who has lived on Sycamore Avenue for 37 years, said the response has been better than anyone expected. Several residents on Sycamore Avenue said they had been waiting since 1984 for something like this.

articles.title: Letter: The Streetlight Upgrade on Pearl Road Needs Attention
body: To the editor: Thank you for printing this letter, and for all the work the paper does to keep us informed.

Please keep the streetlight upgrade in the budget. Many of us on Pearl Road use it every week. To the editor: I have lived on Pearl Road for 31 years, and I want to say what a difference the Canal Park Food Pantry has made.
Sadie Weatherby, Hickory Ridge

articles.title: Letter: Support the Sidewalk Ramp
body: To the editor: I hope the council will listen to the people who turned out at the February meeting.
Please keep the sidewalk ramp in the budget. Many of us on Tillman Road use it every week.

To the editor: I have lived on Tillman Road for 35 years, and I want to say what a difference the Mill Hill Lions Club has made. Thank you for printing this letter, and for all the work the paper does to keep us informed.
Felix Hobart, Mill Hill

articles.title: Foxglove Heights Elementary Students Earn Regional Honors
articles.deck: Principal Patrice Underhill said the school is grateful to families who volunteered this year.
body: Sign-up forms went home in backpacks this week, and the first session is set for January.
Students will meet on Wednesday afternoons in Millrace Green, and transportation will be provided for those who need it.
Principal Patrice Underhill said the program was built with help from parents and local volunteers.
